mappings.evidence: Each chef works on a different dish simultaneously, analogous to each thread executing a separate task.
Chefs prepare dishes independently, just as threads perform independent tasks.
Chefs share these resources and must coordinate access, mirroring threads sharing memory and requiring synchronization.
When two chefs need the same resource, one waits briefly, similar to a thread blocking on a lock.

mappings.source_element: non‑deterministic order of dishes reaching the dining room
mappings.evidence: Customers receive complete meals regardless of order, just as a program’s final result is unchanged despite varied thread interleavings.
The head chef assigns more cooks to busy stations, akin to an OS assigning CPU time to threads for load balancing.

mappings.target_element: parallel execution on multi‑core or distributed systems
mappings.evidence: Parallel work in the kitchen speeds service, just as concurrency improves performance on multi‑core hardware.

result.process_summary: In the analogy, many chefs (threads) independently prepare dishes (tasks) while sharing limited kitchen resources (memory). They coordinate via brief waiting when a resource is contested (synchronization). The order in which dishes reach the dining room is nondeterministic, yet each customer receives a complete meal, mirroring how concurrent threads may interleave arbitrarily but still produce the correct final program state. A head chef (operating system) balances workload across stations, analogous to a scheduler distributing work across cores.
potential_breaks: Physical kitchen resources have spatial constraints that differ from abstract memory models in concurrency.
Chefs can communicate verbally in ways threads cannot, potentially overstating the ease of coordination.
The head chef’s authority is more hierarchical than typical OS scheduling, which is often preemptive and automated.
In a kitchen, some dishes have inherent ordering dependencies (e.g., sauce before plating) that the analogy does not address, whereas concurrency may involve explicit task dependencies.
